subject: Clarifications: logs, backups, and deletion SLAs after demo
messages:
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@medify-health.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medify-health.com
Date: 2027-04-30T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: quick clarifications on logs/backups/deletion SLAs

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning — good demo. A few specific items our security and engineering leads asked to clarify so we can finish our internal risk assessment: 

1) SOC 2 status and expected date for report availability (Type II preferred).
2) HIPAA posture — we will be processing PHI for the pilot; does Redwood have a HIPAA BA and what deployment modes are covered?
3) Log retention: what categories of logs do you retain (access/authorization, application, audit), and what are default retention windows for each?
4) Backups & snapshots: retention windows and whether deleted data may remain in backup snapshots (and for how long).
5) Deletion SLA: when a customer requests data erasure, what is the expected timeline for primary and for backups/archives?
6) Key management: who controls encryption keys (Redwood-managed KMS vs. customer-managed)?

We'd also like to initiate a short vendor security questionnaire. I attached our initial questionnaire to speed things up. Can you confirm the best internal contact to own the questionnaire and provide evidence (SOC2 bridge letter, backup retention matrix, sample deletion playbook)?

Thanks — if it's easier we can do a 30-min follow-up with your security lead.

Best,
Alice Johnson
Head of Security Operations
Medify Health

Attachments: Medify_Security_Q_20270430.xlsx (spreadsheet of vendor questions)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@medify-health.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-30T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick clarifications on logs/backups/deletion SLAs

Hi Alice — thanks for the detailed list and for sharing Medify's questionnaire. Quick recap and proposed next steps below. Long answer in the attached retention summary and our questionnaire template.

Summary answers (short):
- SOC 2: Redwood has completed SOC 2 Type II for our control plane (report available upon NDA). We're currently in the audit cycle for 2027 Q3 for additional cluster controls; expected public availability of the new Type II attestation is Q4 2027. We'll provide a bridge letter and the latest assurance pack as soon as legal signs the disclosure NDA.
- HIPAA: We support customers handling PHI when using Redwood Private (VPC or on-prem). For Hosted API, PHI is supported under a signed BAA with specific configurations; we'll need to confirm your desired deployment model and dataflow.
- Log categories & defaults (proposal):
  * Access & auth logs: default 180 days (configurable to shorter/longer for Dedicated/Private).
  * Application/LLM inference logs (non-content telemetry): default 365 days; content logs are treated according to customer policy and can be disabled or routed to Private.
  * Audit trails (policy changes, config): default 365 days with export to long-term archive on request.
- Backups & snapshots:
  * Short-term snapshots (fast restore) retained by default for 45 days.
  * Optional snapshot archival (cold storage) available for 1–7 years depending on contract.
  * Note: backup snapshots may contain recoverable copies of content for up to the snapshot retention window.
- Deletion SLA (proposed baseline):
  * Primary datastore deletion: completed within 30 days of request (verified by audit log).
  * Snapshot/backup purge: purge requests queued and completed within the snapshot retention window policy; for standard customers we commit to initiating purges within 30 days and completing irreversible removal within 90 days for snapshot data unless archival retention applies.
- Key management: we offer Redwood-managed KMS by default and customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for Private deployments and Enterprise contracts.

Next steps I suggest:
1) We will complete Medify's questionnaire (attached template) and return by COB Thu 5/6.
2) Ben will work with you on pilot retention parameters (we can provision a pilot with the 180/45 baseline and adjust after the security review).
3) Kimberly will provide the SOC2 bridge letter and the retention playbook excerpts for backup deletion flow.

I've attached a short one-page Redwood_Retention_Summary_20270430.pdf and our Redwood_Security_Questionnaire_Template_v1.xlsx to speed review. If these baseline windows work, let's schedule 30 minutes next week (I'm available Tue/Wed).

Looping you both in with a suggested commercial approach based on Sofia's baseline:

- Ask: Offer Medify a pilot with access/auth logs = 180 days and snapshot retention = 45 days (no archival) to reduce exposure and meet their compliance team halfway. Pilot term 60 days so they can validate deletion workflow.
- Risk: Backup purge timelines are the sticky point; legal needs to confirm that our 90-day irreversible window for standard backups is acceptable or whether we need a contractual exception to accelerate eradication for the pilot.
- Action items for Kimberly: Can you confirm we have a SOC 2 bridge letter we can share under NDA and whether the deletion playbook covers emergency purge for snapshots (what steps, who signs off, expected exec SLA)?
- Action items for Sofia: Please confirm proposed wording for the MOU/pilot appendix (retention parameters + deletion SLA + evidence delivery timeline). I'll draft the mutual action plan entry for RDW-2345 once we align.

Quick note: Medify indicated they handle PHI in production; we should make the pilot explicitly non-PHI or ensure BAA is signed before any PHI ingestion.

Thanks — I'll hold off sending the MOU until Kimberly confirms the legal/security bits.

Ben Carter
